rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF SAMMIE JUNE NATHAN
rulings.Calendar Matter: ACCOUNTING PETITION RE: Report, Fees, Final Distribution
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 8/19/26. (No earlier availability.) Issue(s) necessitating continuance: (1) Notice must have attached to it the procedures for how to make a remote appearance by Zoom and CourtCall, as well as remote public access, as set out at https://sf.courts.ca.gov/divisions/probate-court. [LRSF 14.1 C.6.] (2) Attorney costs must be fully itemized, showing the date the costs was paid, the payee, the description (e.g., what was filed that incurred a filing fee), and the amount. ("Reimbursed" costs must be for actual costs advanced, not "estimated remaining e-filing fees." If additional closing costs are anticipated, a reserve should be requested.) (3) Detailed schedules of receipts and gains and losses on sale must be filed to support the statutory fee. [CRC 7.705(b) and 7.550(b)(6).] Please provide a proposed order and courtesy copies of any papers filed to address these issues to the assigned examiner by 8/5/26. After these issues are addressed, an appearance will likely be required in connection with the request for fees for extraordinary services. There were only two, not "multiple", reports of status filed in this case and there were no hearings requiring appearance. This Court does not permit fees for research into routine matters such as addressing a creditor's claim or reviewing the law re sale of real property and disallows internal conferences beyond the least amount of time for an attorney or senior attorney to review the work of a paralegal or associate. The administrator is the sole surviving heir and representative of the other heir; notice of proposed action should not have been required. The fee declaration does not fully address all the requirements of CRC 7.702 (e.g., the nature and difficulty of the tasks performed, results achieved, and the benefit to the estate). Examiner continuances are final and not subject to contest under LRSF 14.10 B. (Item 4 of an I&A should NOT be completed when a probate referee HAS BEEN appointed. In order for this Court to track closed matters, orders to terminate and distribute an estate must begin with the following language: "Order for Final Distribution." [LRSF 14.35 I.6.b.])

rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF NICHOLAS L. JARRETT,
rulings.Calendar Matter: PETITION FOR PROBATE OF WILL AND FOR LETTERS TESTAMENTARY
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 08/04/2026. Issues necessitating continuance: 1) No Duties and Liabilities has been filed (Probate Code Section 8404). 2) The Notice of Petition to Administer Estate does not indicate that the will is lost, that that the petition requests the lost will be admitted to probate, or that IAEA authority is requested (Probate Code Sections 8100 and 9100). 3) A copy of the written statement of the testamentary words, or their substance, or a copy of the lost will, must be attached to the proposed order. An additional hard copy of the lost will must be provided to the clerk for a will file to be created before the hearing to admit the lost will to probate (LRSF 14.20). 4) If a will names a trust or trustee as a devisee, the trustee(s) must be clearly identified in item 8. Where the personal representative and the sole trustee are the same person, or if there is no trustee, the beneficiaries of the trust must be clearly identified. (Probate Code Section 1208(b) and LRSF 14.18.C.2). 5) When second generation or more distant heirs are listed, the deceased ancestor(s) through whom they take (or would have taken) must be named, the relationship(s) to the decedent stated, and the date(s) of death specified (LRSF 14.18.C.3). 6) The date of death must be specified for all deceased devisees and heirs (14.18.D.1). Please indicate Donald George Stroh's date of death. If Donald Stroh postdeceased decedent, please review LRSF 14.18.D.3. Please address the above issues and deliver courtesy copies of all further filings no later than 07/21/2026 to avoid additional continuance.

rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF YAN YAN JULIA WU
rulings.Calendar Matter: PETITION FOR LETTERS OF ADMINISTRATION
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 8/18/26. (No earlier availability.) Issue(s) necessitating continuance: (1) An amended petition was just filed on 6/29/26, which was not at least 15 days before this hearing in order for notice to be sufficient. (2) An amended pleading requires the same notice of hearing (including publication) as the pleading it amends. [CRC 7.53(a).] The mailed and published notice must clearly show that an AMENDED PETITION has been filed and will be heard on 8/18/26. (3) Notice must have attached to it the procedures for how to make a remote appearance by Zoom and CourtCall, as well as remote public access, as set out at https://sf.courts.ca.gov/divisions/probate-court. [LRSF 14.1 C.6.] (4) When second generation or more distant heirs are listed, the deceased ancestor through whom they take (or would have taken) shall be named and his or her date of death and relationship to the decedent shall be stated. [LRSF 14.18 C.] Who were the decedent's parents and when did they die? (5) Item 2 of the Acknowledgment of Receipt of the Duties and Liabilities requires the telephone number, too. Please provide a new (complete) proposed order and courtesy copies of the amended petition and any papers filed to address these issues to the assigned examiner by 8/7/26. (A proposed order must be complete in itself in that it must set forth... all matters actually passed on by the Court, such as: the date of the hearing, necessary findings, the relief granted, the names of the interested parties, and descriptions of property or amounts of money affected. A proposed order must be drafted so that its general effect may be determined without reference to the petition on which it is based and must include only those findings requested in the petition. [LRSF 14.7 A.2. and 3.]) Examiner continuances are final and not subject to contest under LRSF 14.10 B.
